A particle moves with position $x(t)=3\cos t$, $y(t)=3\sin t$. Find its speed at any time $t$, and interpret the result.
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=-3\sin t$, $\frac{dy}{dt}=3\cos t$. Speed $=\sqrt{9\sin^2t+9\cos^2t}=\sqrt{9}=3$ (constant). The particle traces a circle of radius $3$ at constant speed.

questions.q: Eliminate the parameter from $x(t)=t$, $y(t)=t^2-1$ to find the Cartesian equation, and sketch it.
questions.answer: Since $x=t$, substitute directly: $y=x^2-1$, an upward parabola shifted down $1$ unit.

questions.q: Eliminate the parameter from $x(t)=2t+1$, $y(t)=4t-3$ to find the Cartesian equation.
questions.answer: From $x=2t+1$: $t=\frac{x-1}{2}$. Substitute: $y=4\left(\frac{x-1}{2}\right)-3=2(x-1)-3=2x-5$. A line with slope $2$.

questions.q: Explain why eliminating the parameter from $x(t)=\cos t$, $y(t)=\sin t$ using the identity $\sin^2t+\cos^2t=1$ gives a relation that is NOT a function $y=f(x)$.
questions.answer: Substituting gives $x^2+y^2=1$, the equation of a unit circle. For most $x$-values in $(-1,1)$, there are two corresponding $y$-values ($\pm\sqrt{1-x^2}$), so this relation fails the vertical line test and is not a function of $x$.

questions.q: For $x(t)=t^2$, $y(t)=t^3$ (with $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\frac{3}{4t}$ found earlier), determine the concavity of the curve for $t>0$ and for $t<0$.
questions.answer: For $t>0$: $\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\frac{3}{4t}>0$, so the curve is concave up. For $t<0$: $\frac{3}{4t}<0$, so the curve is concave down.

questions.q: For $x(t)=t^2-4$, $y(t)=t^3-3t$, find the value(s) of $t$ where the tangent line is horizontal (where $\frac{dy}{dt}=0$, provided $\frac{dx}{dt}\neq0$).
questions.answer: $\frac{dy}{dt}=3t^2-3=0 \Rightarrow t=\pm1$. Check $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t$: at $t=\pm1$, $\frac{dx}{dt}=\pm2\neq0$, so both give valid horizontal tangents.

questions.q: For the same curve, find the value(s) of $t$ where the tangent line is vertical (where $\frac{dx}{dt}=0$, provided $\frac{dy}{dt}\neq0$).
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t=0 \Rightarrow t=0$. Check $\frac{dy}{dt}=3(0)^2-3=-3\neq0$, so $t=0$ gives a valid vertical tangent, at the point $x(0)=-4$, $y(0)=0$.

questions.q: A particle's position is $x(t)=t^2$, $y(t)=t^3-3t$ for $t\in[-2,2]$. Find all times when the particle is moving straight up or down (vertical velocity component only, i.e. $\frac{dx}{dt}=0$).
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=2t=0 \Rightarrow t=0$. At $t=0$: position is $(0,0)$, and the particle is momentarily moving purely vertically (since horizontal velocity is $0$ there).

sections.heading: Arc length of a full circle (verifying the circumference formula)

questions.q: Use the parametric arc length formula to verify that the circumference of a circle $x(t)=r\cos t$, $y(t)=r\sin t$ for $t\in[0,2\pi]$ is $2\pi r$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=-r\sin t$, $\frac{dy}{dt}=r\cos t$. $L=\int_0^{2\pi}\sqrt{r^2\sin^2t+r^2\cos^2t}\,dt=\int_0^{2\pi}r\,dt=r(2\pi)=2\pi r$, matching the known circumference formula.

questions.q: Find the arc length of the parametric curve $x(t)=e^t\cos t$, $y(t)=e^t\sin t$ is a spiral; set up (but do not evaluate) its arc length integral on $[0,\pi]$.
questions.answer: $\frac{dx}{dt}=e^t\cos t-e^t\sin t$, $\frac{dy}{dt}=e^t\sin t+e^t\cos t$. After simplification, $\left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)^2+\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)^2=2e^{2t}$. So $L=\int_0^{\pi}\sqrt{2e^{2t}}\,dt=\int_0^{\pi}e^t\sqrt{2}\,dt$.

questions.q: A Ferris wheel of radius $10$ m completes one revolution every $40$ s, centered $12$ m above the ground. Write parametric equations for a rider's height above the ground as a function of time $t$ (seconds), assuming the rider starts at the bottom.
questions.answer: Angular speed $=\frac{2\pi}{40}=\frac{\pi}{20}$ rad/s. Starting at the bottom means height $=12-10\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{20}t\right)$ (using $x(t)=t$ for time, $y(t)=12-10\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{20}t\right)$ for height).
